chapter: Opening, arrival in Los Angeles and the Quality Four
title: First Black radio broadcast on KFWB; Sue Hoye
summary: Mrs. Howard says the Quality Four were the first Negroes to broadcast on Warner Brothers' station; she sang under the name Sue Hoye, and recounts the move from the Hummingbird to the Nightingale.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: The Quality Four were the first Negroes that for Warner Brothers, when they first had their radio station, did a session on the radio.
How did that come about?
Well, it came about -- someone came down to the cafe, and heard them.
I forgot about it.
And (inaudible).
How about that? That's really -- yeah.
That's right. She had it. I forget all them things.
Well, you're remembering good, too.
Carolyn Snowden and myself, and a girl named Arlene Johnson, we were entertainers down there, and we
went to the studio.
And don't forget Sue Hoye.
Sue Hoye?
Yeah.
That's the name I went by.
No kidding.
Sue Hoye.
Oh, you've been mentioned before. I believe Lawrence Brown mentioned you. You sang, right?
And we were the first to sing over the Warner Brothers radio, when they first opened that station.
Would that have been KFWB? Was that the station?
Yeah, that's what it was, KFWB.
I guess it was. I guess it was.
So that would be about what year?

Oh, that was in '24, because we were still the Hummingbird -- see, we left the Hummingbirds in the first part of '25, because Dr. Nelson, who owned the Hummingbirds, he opened this cafe, the Nightingale, on Washington Boulevard. And that's when he sent for Paul and them, that's when the show broke up in Amarillo. And he sent for the band to come there and open a new show at the Cafe Nightingale. And he brought them back here.
Cut if off.
